profile.campus: Altoona, Polk County, Iowa (Meta's Altoona data center campus, seven Meta-tagged buildings on OpenStreetMap; Meta's own reporting describes the campus as still expanding)

profile.reading:
This is Facebook/Meta Altoona Data Center 2 on Meta's Altoona, Iowa campus. Meta broke ground on the Altoona campus in 2013 and has expanded it seven times since, most recently announced in December 2024, per Meta's own fact sheet and Data Center Frontier's reporting; Meta has invested more than $2.5 billion in the city of Altoona and the state of Iowa through this campus. Construction has employed an average of about 1,000 workers a year over twelve years, totaling 8.7 million work-hours, with peak skilled-trade staffing of 1,300 workers; day-to-day operations employ more than 400 people. Meta reports operational buildings on the campus are LEED Gold certified, that it matches all of its global electricity use with 100% clean and renewable energy, and that a Meta-supported project added 225 megawatts of new renewable generation capacity in Iowa. Meta says it has made more than 300 grants and sponsorships in the area since 2015 and provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Polk County-area schools and nonprofits. Meta does not publish a specific street address, building count, or per-building square footage for individual Altoona structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

Iowa has drawn more than $17 billion in data center capital investment, with 27 data centers operating or under construction statewide as of 2025, according to Inside Climate News; Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Apple together account for nearly all of that total. The state has led the nation in wind generation since adopting the first state renewable portfolio standard in 1983, with wind now supplying about 60% of Iowa's electricity and helping keep industrial power prices among the eighth-lowest in the country, both factors regional reporting ties directly to hyperscale operators' site selection in the Altoona/Des Moines corridor. That same reporting states Meta's Altoona campus has used up to 16% of the city of Altoona's water supply and consumed roughly 1.2 million megawatt-hours of electricity annually, and flags that federal cuts to clean-energy tax incentives under the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act are projected by Energy Innovation to raise Iowa industrial electricity rates by 14 to 26 percent, a risk regional press has connected to the pace of further hyperscale investment in the state.

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity, square footage, or a building count for the Altoona campus; regional press (Data Center Frontier, citing Meta's own December 2024 announcement) reports the campus as a whole will exceed 5 million square feet on completion, expected in 2025, making it Meta's largest data center campus worldwide, surpassing Prineville, Oregon's 4.6 million square feet. No per-building figure is asserted here.

profile.regional_context: Altoona sits in the Des Moines metro area of central Iowa. Meta chose the site in part for MidAmerican Energy's wind-heavy generation mix and Iowa's wind-energy tax credits; MidAmerican has said it supplies its Iowa customers, Meta included, with wind generation matching 100% of retail load on an annual basis. Iowa's data center cluster in the Altoona/Des Moines area also includes Microsoft, Google, and Apple facilities, and the sector has become a significant driver of the state's industrial electricity demand and a subject of debate over local property-tax abatement policy, according to Inside Climate News and the Bend Bulletin-style local reporting seen in other Meta markets.

reading.body:
Meta has invested $2.5B and committed over a decade to this Polk County campus since groundbreaking in 2013, signaling sustained confidence in Iowa for hyperscale compute infrastructure. The operator publishes no IT load capacity for this facility, so its size relative to other Meta campuses and to the grid constraint cannot be assessed from disclosed figures. Operational buildings achieve LEED Gold certification. Meta does not publish a specific street address, building count, or square footage for this campus.

Iowa has published power capacity for only two data center facilities statewide, totaling 18 MW of disclosed IT load across 52 mapped sites. This campus ranks third by published megawatts in the state, a ranking that reflects the rarity of public disclosure rather than confirmed capacity. The state context provided does not establish how much load this facility represents or how it compares to the unmeasured capacity at the other 51 mapped facilities.

Meta reports electricity use matched with 100 percent clean and renewable energy and has funded a 225 megawatt renewable energy project in Iowa as part of meeting its net-zero operations goal. The campus employs 400 plus operational staff once complete and drew peak construction labor of 1,300 skilled workers. Without published power figures, the relevance of this campus to grid constraints on AI scaling cannot be determined from available data.
